summary: Zimbabwe seeks to raise forest land to 10.4 million ha by 2025, add 100,000 ha of natural forest annually in 2021–2025, and expand plantations to 118,848 ha; reported additions differ: 10,000 versus 7,000 ha/year. It plans 2,000 ha/year of native-tree planting on degraded or fallow land and 5,000 ha/year of exotic trees in tobacco areas. Conservation pledges seek a 500,000 ha burning reduction over 2020–2025, including annual cuts of 50,000 ha in natural forest, 30,000 ha in wooded grassland and 2,000 ha in plantations. Agricultural and agroforestry measures include conservation tillage and solar irrigation on 200,000 ha each by 2035, 20% organic-matter composting, 12% energy savings by 2030, improved feed and health for 5% and 10% of cattle, 0.3 ha of trees per ha of tobacco, and 10 fruit trees per household. The forest goal is 87.3% of 2022 mapped forest; the burning target covers 3.46% of mapped agriculture.
